- [USER] User recalled the visual effects in Inception being mind-blowing and asked about behind-the-scenes footage.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The visual effects in Inception were impressive and groundbreaking, using a blend of practical effects and CGI.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Techniques used included changing gravity, rotating environments, and folding architecture, with motion control, miniature models, and extensive green screen work.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Christopher Nolan, the director, preferred practical effects over CGI, with many effects being real and practical.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The zero-gravity scene involved building a rotating set and filming actors suspended on cables.
- [USER] User expressed interest in the rotating set for the zero-gravity scene and asked how long it took to film that scene.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The zero-gravity sequence took six weeks to film and is considered one of the most memorable sequences in the film.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The rotating set was built at Cardington Studios in Bedfordshire, England, one of the largest enclosed spaces in Europe.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Several other scenes in the film also had impressive visual effects and took considerable time to create.
